headline: Common Gas Range Issues: When to Call Alpha-Plumbing
articleBody: It's super common for gas ranges to have hiccups, but knowing which ones need a professional touch is key for both performance and safety. You might notice your burners aren't igniting consistently, or maybe they're producing weak or unusually colored flames – like yellow or orange instead of a crisp blue. This often signals an issue with the gas flow or the burner itself, possibly due to a blocked gas port or a faulty igniter. Another big one is if you can smell gas when the range isn't in use, or if the smell is unusually strong when it is. This is a critical safety concern and you should address it immediately. If your oven isn't heating evenly or reaching the set temperature, it could point to a problem with the oven's gas valve or igniter. And, of course, any visible damage to the gas line connection behind the range means you need professional help pronto.
